results.label: this tree ships the M112 trading-window module (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the module names exactly four states, and `unset` is not one of the two refusals
no window selected is `unset`, blocks nothing, and says so
a window containing the trader’s local time is `inside` and blocks nothing
a window that cannot contain it is `outside` and DOES block — the hard block, not a penalty
the refusal names the window, the zone, the local time there and the minutes until it opens — never a generic phrase
and it carries his own rationale for a boundary he calls a cheat code
the start minute is INSIDE the window
the end minute is OUTSIDE it — the window ends when the clock reaches its end
a start later than the end runs through midnight on purpose (one Asia window, not two)
and just before that wrapped start is inside it
a malformed stored clock is `unavailable` — a refusal with a repair action, never a silent pass
one side without the other is unreadable rather than half a window
two equal times are refused rather than read as "all day"
a window with no zone at all is unreadable, and the sentence says nothing is inferred from the server clock or a session label
a missing server clock is unavailable too, not an assumed instant
`safeState` cannot throw: even a stored row whose field explodes on read comes back as the module’s own refusal
the time parser accepts exactly HH:MM and coerces nothing else (surrounding blanks are trimmed, the clock itself is not guessed)
and blank means "not set" rather than invalid, so clearing a window is a real choice
a window authored in a zone the trader has since changed is UNAVAILABLE, and both zones are named — a hard boundary never moves on a new clock
an offset or abbreviation is not a zone: the module would not follow its daylight-saving rule
the zone actually drives the answer: the same pair is outside at one instant and inside at another
the suggestion is labelled as the trader’s own recorded journal, with the bucket, the count and the floor
it is explicitly NOT a prediction, an edge or a permission, and it is not applied by the module
below the course’s 30-trade review floor nothing is suggested at all — the description is withheld rather than presented as a window
with no closed recorded session there is nothing to derive, and it says which fact is missing
without the trader’s own zone the suggestion is refused rather than computed on another clock
entries spread around the clock yield NO single band rather than a stretched one
a band around midnight is ONE band on the clock, not a 0-width or inside-out pair
the band is the middle 50 % of the recorded hours, rounded outward to whole hours
a blocking window becomes the SAME kind of stop the personal guardrails produce, and it cannot be overridden
an unreadable window blocks as its own rule, so a repair is named rather than a boundary invented
`unset` is published and blocks nothing — the difference between "you selected none" and "it could not be read" survives the merge
an existing stop is never hidden: the window appends its own breach and can only make the refusal stricter
the module writes nothing: no store, no clock, no counter is touched by an evaluation
and the settings note warns without repairing: a window covering most of the clock is reported, not shortened

scope: M112 portability: the rule is the file: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
